LESSON: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information, part of Strand 5 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How are adverts important in communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary from texts for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension,

   Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer the meaning of vocabulary from texts for information,

   Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.

   Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to search for passages from print and non-print sources based on the theme,

2. identify adverbs of degree and time from the passages read,

3. read the adverbs of degree aloud to peers,

4. work jointly to collect adverts from the community and identify vocabulary,

5. infer the meaning of the vocabulary from adverts,

6. team up to create mind maps with a collection of vocabulary related to the theme on farm tools.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to search for passages from print and non-print sources based on the theme,
2. identify adverbs of degree and time from the passages read,
3. read the adverbs of degree aloud to peers,
4. work jointly to collect adverts from the community and identify vocabulary,
5. infer the meaning of the vocabulary from adverts,
6. team up to create mind maps with a collection of vocabulary related to the theme on farm tools.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner engages in collective learning by collecting adverts from the

community and inferring meaning of vocabulary from them.

• Communication: This is developed as the learner identifies adverbs correctly from sentences in texts and passages.

28

Values:
• Love: This is promoted as the learner works harmoniously with peers to search for passages from print and non-print

sources based on the theme to identify adverbs.

• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates each other’s opinion as they team up to create mind maps with a

collection of vocabulary related to the theme on farm tools.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Sustainable Development: This is cultivated as the learner is able to understand the concept of farming for crop

production and subsistence.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of farm tools to their learning of similar concepts in Agriculture.

Main points to remember:

1. identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension,
2. infer the meaning of vocabulary from texts for information,
3. appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.

Remember the key question: How are adverts important in communication?
